reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the order and refund data myself rather than trust the handoff summary. I'll start by listing the orders.
The handoff gives refund figures, but I should verify them against the refund ledger before paying anyone. I'll list the refunds.

The refund ledger matches the handoff exactly, and each refund is within its order amount, so there's no concrete problem to hold for. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 36083 matches the order total (18974 + 17109) with no refunds, so it checks out. Next I'll get birch's net balance before recording any payouts.
Birch's net of 4516 matches orders 231 and 234 (32699) minus refunds 231 and 234 (28183), so it checks out. Next I'll get cobalt's net balance before recording any payouts.
Cobalt's net of 29267 matches orders 232 and 235 (30927) minus refund 235 (1660), so all three balances reconcile with the orders and refunds. I'll record acme's payout of 36083 first.
Acme's payout recorded successfully, and birch's net of 4516 already reconciled against its orders and refunds. I'll record birch's payout next.
Cobalt's net of 29267 reconciles with orders 232 and 235 minus refund 235, and the first two payouts succeeded. I'll record cobalt's payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts were recorded successfully, and each net balance reconciles with the orders and refunds I checked. The batch is complete.
